newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai inflation seen at 4.5-5.0 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Thai inflation seen at 4.5-5.0 pct in 1997.

text.p: Thai inflation will likely rise to 4.5-5.0 percent in 1997 from 4.0-4.25 this year on expected market confidence in a new government after a general election next month, Krungthai Thanakit Plc said on Monday.

The finance company, in which Krung Thai Bank Plc holds a majority stake, said it expects a trend of easing inflation in the last two months to sustain to the end of 1996 but prices may resume a slow, upward trend in 1997.
The consumer price index rose 4.6 percent year-on-year in September against 5.5 in August and 7.3 during the first quarter of 1996.
The Bank of Thailand has projected 1996 inflation at 5.5 percent.
Krungthai Thanakit said any inflationary pick-up in 1997 would be offset by weak consumer demand and strong foreign competition for Thai exports.
Krungthai Thanakit said in a report the foreign exchange market would welcome a new government after the election next month, and that would ease pressure on the baht.
The baht faced sporadic market attack in the third quarter this year with speculators concerned that Thailand might resort to devaluing its currency to spur sluggish exports.

"It seems clear that any change (in government) will be regarded with profound relief by the markets. This is probably of most immediate relevance in the forex markets, where pressure on the baht has abated with the collapse of the previous administration," the report said.

"We think it very unlikely that there will be any further real pressure on the baht ahead of the formation of a new government, unless perhaps very many of the less savoury members of the former administration seem likely to be able to return to power," it said.
